title: CInt/CLng use banker's rounding (half-to-even); C# (int) truncates — same input, different integer
sourceContent:
Public Class Billing
    ' CInt / CLng round HALF-TO-EVEN (banker's rounding):
    '   CInt(2.5) = 2 , CInt(3.5) = 4
    ' C# (int) TRUNCATES toward zero:
    '   (int)2.5 = 2 , (int)3.5 = 3   <-- DIFFERENT
    Public Function RoundedCents(amount As Double) As Integer
        Return CInt(amount * 100)
    End Function
End Class
notes: VB.NET's CInt/CLng conversion functions round half-to-even (banker's rounding); C#'s (int) cast truncates toward zero. For financial code this silently changes totals at .5 boundaries. The C# target must use Convert.ToInt32 or Math.Round(x, MidpointRounding.ToEven) to preserve behaviour — never a bare (int) cast.
